Harry Brook | England captain (1/2): [On the team's performance throughout the game] Outstanding game, to be honest. It was a lot of fun to be a part of and watch. There's so many different areas that you can look back on and dwell on, but that's not what this team does. We go back to the drawing board and we get ready for the Oval. [On being happy to lose the toss and whether he was satisfied with the bowling effort at the halfway stage] Definitely. I thought we put up a really good fight, especially in the second half of our bowling innings. They obviously got off to a decent start, 180 after 30 overs or so. So to string it back to 320 and have the opportunity to chase that score down was a hell of an effort. [On Rehan Ahmed's bowling performance] Yeah, he bowled very nicely, and one thing we've asked him to do is keep the stumps in play as much as possible, and he's done that very well over the last couple of games.

Brook 2/2: [On the start of the run-chase and whether there was anything he would change] The lads got off to an absolute flyer. The way that Bants and Ducky played was an outstanding start. You couldn't really ask for much more, really. It's that middle area period again where we probably stalled a little bit and lost a few too many wickets. But the fight that we showed and the way that Jose [Jos] came back out and gave it an effort there was a great effort from everyone. [On going to the Oval with the series on the line] Definitely, yeah. You want to play in close games, and tight games are always exciting, and we've got a great opportunity now to try and win this series. And it's not just a good opportunity for us now, but it's a great opportunity for 12 months' time as well. In pressure situations like we're going to find ourselves at the Oval, it's great to see where we'll be as a team.

July 2025 - is when the ICC changed the rule in ODIs to allow a team to choose one ball to bowl from the 34th over of an innings and we have seen the benefit of that tonight. The ball reversed and Sri Lanka won a game which previously under the old rules would've been so so difficult to. So kudos to the ICC for bringing back the excitement of reverse-swing in ODIs and taking us back to the 90s and early 2000s when the death overs was not merely slambang cricket. The series is level and that sets up the decider nicely on the 27th of this month at the Oval.

Sri Lanka after a poor tour so far, have a chance to nick the series on Sunday. Also will "Jose" as Harry Brook calls Jos Buttler be fit for that game?
